seoTitle: Scatter Plot Maker with Trendline and Correlation r
metaDescription: Paste x and y pairs to draw a scatter plot with a least-squares trendline, slope, intercept, Pearson r and R squared. Free, in your browser.
intro: Plots paired numbers as points, fits an ordinary least-squares line and reports slope, intercept, Pearson correlation r and R squared.
why:
A scatter plot answers whether two measures move together. The trendline and r make that concrete, and the data table keeps every point readable without sight.

The fit is simple linear regression of y on x. It says nothing about causation, and a high r can come from one outlier, so look at the plot before trusting the number. Axes use rounded tick values and the chart is plain SVG you can restyle.
howTo: Paste two columns, x then y. A header row sets the axis names.
Leave the trendline on or turn it off.
Read the equation, r and R squared printed on the chart.

faq.a: Pearson r runs from -1 to 1. Near 0 means no straight-line relationship; the sign gives the direction.
Ordinary least squares of y on x, with all points weighted equally.

faq.q: Can it plot groups in colours?
faq.a: Not in this tool. Use the bubble chart for a third variable.
Yes against a hand calculation in Python for the sample data; it matches to all shown digits.
